verses.author: model_A
verses.text: An orchard planted by a man who never tasted its fruit.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
still, the branches bend
toward whatever hands come next,
not knowing whose they'll be

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
morning frost lets go
the way it always meant to—
someone else's warmth

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
not the sun's promise
just the way ice trusts the light
to finish what it starts

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the ladder left leaning
against a tree still growing—
someone will need it

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I didn't plant this
but I'll water what comes up,
call it mine for now

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the borrowed rake, returned
still holding a few leaves
that weren't there before

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
dust on the windowsill
where I keep meaning to write
someone else's name

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the kettle's whistle
answers a question I asked
myself, twice removed

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
what I inherited
I keep in a drawer I never
open, but never sell

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
morning frost melts first
where his boot prints marked the snow
gone before noon

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the phone call I didn't make
still ringing somewhere
in a house I don't live in anymore

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a spider rebuilds
in the corner I keep sweeping —
who's teaching whom

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the drawer I never open
hums faintly at night —
maybe it's just the house settling

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the moon takes its turn
peering into rooms we've locked —
even it forgets which key

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
frost on the window
where someone traced a name —
morning erases the argument
